evidence.finding: The sheet provides a JSON request, DataWeave transformation, and canonical JSON output.
The canonical message is transformed into a target JSON request.
Classification values are mapped to target classification identifiers.

assumptions.statement: Confirm the operator and private-network execution environment for the Source helper; it sends sanitized service requests to the service-requests queue using Microsoft Entra authentication.
Confirm the mock target consumer's message contract and ownership; the lab does not require real external-system accounts or credentials.
DataWeave behavior will be reimplemented and tested rather than executed directly.

The Source tab's canonical Output feeds Canonical to target Input via canonical-requests/target-transform. Confirm the link against sanitized payload evidence and any available architecture diagram; do not infer it from tab order.
A mock consumer of target-requests/mock-target verifies the final Output. Confirm mock-consumer ownership and duplicate-handling behavior before testing.

flows.name: service-request-to-canonical
flows.trigger: Receive and lock from Service Bus queue service-requests
steps: Implement only the processing tab Source requests to canonical.
Provide a parameterized Source helper that sends its sanitized Input fixture to service-requests with content type, message ID, and correlation ID.
Validate the inbound Input against its payload contract.
Apply this tab's transformation rules to produce and validate the canonical Output.
Publish Output to canonical-requests; subscription target-transform supplies the Canonical to target workflow.
Complete the service-requests message only after successful publication.
flows.failureBehavior: Do not complete Input on validation, transformation, or publication failure. Apply bounded retries and dead-letter policy; preserve correlation and handle duplicates if publication succeeds but completion fails.

flows.name: canonical-to-target
flows.trigger: Receive and lock from Service Bus topic canonical-requests, subscription target-transform
steps: Implement only the processing tab Canonical to target.
Validate canonical Input against this tab's payload contract.
Apply transformation rules and classification lookups to produce and validate target Output; any XRef entries are lookup artifacts, not workflows.
Publish Output to target-requests for the mock-target subscription.
Complete the target-transform message only after successful publication.
flows.failureBehavior: Do not complete Input on invalid canonical data, unmapped classification, or failed Output publication. Apply bounded retries and dead-letter policy and record only sanitized diagnostics and correlation identifiers.

azureResources.type: Private Logic App Standard hosting foundation
azureResources.purpose: Host both tab workflows with the workshop network and keyless host-storage baseline.
One workflow for Source requests to canonical and one for Canonical to target; informational architecture and XRef tabs do not become workflows.
Provide durable Source ingress and topic/subscription handoffs with the approved private connectivity and a topic-capable SKU.
Receive sanitized Input messages from the Source helper for the Source workflow.

azureResources.type: Service Bus topic canonical-requests and subscription target-transform
azureResources.purpose: Route the Source workflow's canonical Output to Canonical to target Input.

azureResources.type: Service Bus topic target-requests and subscription mock-target
azureResources.purpose: Expose the last processing tab's target Output to the approved mock consumer.
Record correlated operational telemetry without full payloads.
Reference an external-system credential only if managed identity or federation is unavailable.
Not selected for broker-based Source helper ingress; consider only if a separately approved API ingress requirement exists.

identityBoundaries.identity: Source helper operator's Microsoft Entra identity

identityBoundaries.scope: Separate assignments at the input queue and input subscription; shared site identity, not per-workflow identities
Separate assignments at each output topic

identityBoundaries.identity: Approved mock consumer or mock adapter identity

identityBoundaries.permissions: Blob, Queue, and Table Data Contributor
Only the data-plane roles required by the approved implementation

reliability: Confirm lock duration and renewal, retry limits, maximum delivery count, TTL, and dead-letter ownership before implementation.
Complete each Input only after publishing validated Output; failed publication leaves Input unsettled for the approved failure policy.
Use stable message IDs and explicit duplicate handling for retries and replay, including publication success followed by completion failure.
Define target timeouts and classify transient versus permanent failures.
Disable unsafe automatic retries for non-idempotent target writes unless an idempotency key is confirmed.
Preserve one correlation identifier through the Source helper, both tab workflows, every broker handoff, and the approved mock consumer.
observability: Record workflow, stage, duration, result, and correlation identifier.
Do not record complete source, canonical, or target payloads.
Create a failure query and alert only after expected volume and support ownership are known.
security: Use HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later.
Keep Logic App host storage private and keyless.
Use Microsoft Entra authentication for the Source helper and managed identity for workflow broker access; confirm private-network reachability without weakening public-access policy.
Do not place external-system credentials, callback URLs, or customer payloads in source, outputs, state, or telemetry.

implementationStages.outcome: Approve the evidence, assumptions, service selection, and target contract.
Deploy the private Logic App Standard and observability foundation.
Deploy approved Service Bus entities, routing, private connectivity, and least-privilege workload and helper access.
Implement two tab workflows, tested transformations and lookup artifacts, and a Source helper against sanitized fixtures and a mock subscriber.
Exercise the approved mock consumer and prove end-to-end success and failure behavior.

validation: Compare transformation outputs with workbook examples.
Verify one workflow per processing tab and no workflow for architecture or XRef information.
Run the Source helper and trace service-requests to canonical-requests/target-transform to target-requests/mock-target with one correlation ID.
Verify upstream Output satisfies downstream Input; test lookup misses, failed publication, duplicate delivery, routing, and dead-letter behavior.
Run Bicep or Terraform format, validation, and deployment preview.
Test success, invalid input, unmapped classification, timeout, transient failure, and permanent target failure.
